content: Hydrogen peroxide mouthwash is an antiseptic approved by the FDA for the removal of secretions associated with a sore mouth. Common adverse reactions include skin irritation, irritation of the skin and mucous membranes, and hypertrophy of tongue papillae with prolonged use. For adults, the FDA-approved indication is to aid in the removal of secretions associated with a sore mouth. The recommended dosage is to use up to four times daily or as directed by a dentist or doctor. Adults and children aged 2 years and older should rinse their mouth with 1/2 tablespoon of the solution for approximately one minute and then expectorate. Children under 12 years of age should be supervised when using this product. For children under 2 years of age, consultation with a dentist or doctor is advised. There is limited information regarding off-label uses of hydrogen peroxide mouthwash in both adults and pediatric patients, whether guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported. Contraindications for hydrogen peroxide mouthwash are not well-documented in the drug label. Warnings include discontinuing use and consulting a doctor if sore mouth symptoms do not improve within seven days, or if swelling, rash, fever, irritation, pain, or redness persists or worsens. Adverse reactions reported in clinical trials and postmarketing experiences are limited in the drug label. Similarly, there is limited information on drug interactions. There is no FDA guidance on the use of hydrogen peroxide mouthwash during pregnancy, labor and delivery, or in nursing mothers. It is also not specifically addressed for pediatric, geriatric, gender-specific, racial, renal impairment, hepatic impairment, or immunocompromised populations. The administration of hydrogen peroxide mouthwash is oral, and there is limited information on monitoring requirements. There is no data on IV compatibility, chronic overdose, pharmacology, mechanism of action, structure, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, or nonclinical toxicology in the drug label. Clinical studies, storage information, and patient counseling details are also limited. The interaction between alcohol and hydrogen peroxide mouthwash has not been established, and patients are advised to consult their doctor regarding alcohol use with this medication. Brand names and look-alike drug names for hydrogen peroxide mouthwash are not well-documented in the drug label.
